source: NCERT Class X, Democratic Politics II, Political Science Ch. 2.

sections.heading: 1. What is Federalism?
points: **Federalism** = a system of government where power is **divided between a central authority and various constituent units** (states).
There are **two or more levels/tiers** of government; each has its own **jurisdiction** in law-making, taxation and administration, guaranteed by the **constitution**.

Two kinds: **'coming together' federations** (independent states unite, e.g. USA, Australia, Switzerland — equal states) and **'holding together' federations** (a large country divides power between states, e.g. **India, Spain, Belgium** — central government often more powerful).

sections.heading: 2. Federalism in the Indian Constitution

sub: **Union List** — subjects of national importance (defence, foreign affairs, banking, currency) — only the **Centre** legislates.
**State List** — subjects of state/local importance (police, trade, agriculture, irrigation) — only **States** legislate.
**Concurrent List** — both Centre and States (education, forest, marriage, adoption); if conflict, the **Union law prevails**.

points: **Residuary subjects** (not in any list) → the **Union** government legislates.
Not all units have equal powers: **special status** (e.g. earlier J&K) and **Union Territories** (governed directly by the Centre).

sections.heading: 3. Making Federalism Work — Language & Centre-State Relations
points: **Linguistic states** — states reorganised on the basis of language (after 1956) strengthened unity, not weakened it.
**Language policy** — **Hindi** is the official language, but not the national language; **22 Scheduled Languages**; English continues as an associate/official language; no single language imposed.

**Centre-State relations** — became more balanced with the rise of **coalition governments** and regional parties (since 1990); use of Article 356 (President's Rule) declined after the **Sarkaria Commission** and Supreme Court rulings.

sections.heading: 4. Decentralisation and Local Government
points: **Decentralisation** = a **third tier** — power taken from Centre/States and given to **local government**.
**73rd (rural — Panchayati Raj) and 74th (urban — municipalities) Constitutional Amendments (1992)**: made local self-government constitutional.
Features: **regular elections** (State Election Commission), **reservation** of seats for SC/ST/OBC and **one-third for women**, and a **State Finance Commission**.
Three-tier Panchayati Raj: **Gram Panchayat → Panchayat Samiti (block) → Zilla Parishad (district)**; **Gram Sabha** = all voters of a village.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: 'Coming together' = USA (equal states); 'holding together' = India (strong Centre).
Three lists: Union, State, Concurrent; residuary powers → Union; Union law prevails on Concurrent conflicts.
Hindi = official language (not national); 22 Scheduled Languages.
73rd Amendment = rural (Panchayati Raj); 74th = urban (municipalities), 1992.
One-third seats reserved for women in local bodies; Gram Sabha = all village voters.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Residuary powers** belong to the **Union** government.
In the **Concurrent List**, if laws clash, the **Union law prevails**.
**73rd Amendment = Panchayats (rural)**, **74th = Municipalities (urban)** — do not swap.
**Hindi** is the **official language, NOT the national language**.
